item.title: CORPORATE GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS INTERN
item.description:
HII is America's largest shipbuilder and a global, all-domain defense provider with a 140-year history of advancing U.S. national defense. This is a 2027 Government Affairs summer internship (minimum 10 weeks) at HII's corporate office in Arlington, Virginia. The intern supports the Government and Customer Relations (GCR) team, whose work is connected to HII's Washington, DC office, and gains exposure to business, finance, information technology, legal and government affairs while supporting the leaders driving HII's future.
Key responsibilities: Support the GCR team through assignments related to policy analysis, legislative affairs and political affairs. Conduct research on legislative bills and activity related to defense issues. Attend congressional hearings and think tank events focused on national security and write summary reports. Assist with Political Action Committee (PAC) recruitment and operational projects. Create key presentations and manage assignments that support GCR's mission and annual deliverables.
Qualifications: Minimum cumulative GPA of 3.0 or higher (official transcripts required). Enrolled in a relevant degree program, typically business, management, accounting, economics/finance, tax accounting, computer information science or information technology, communications, marketing, English, or human resources. Currently attending a 4-year college or university (or 2+2 program), ideally a rising junior or above who returns to school in the fall after the internship, or currently enrolled in a relevant master's program. Ability to work a 40-hour week for a minimum of 10 weeks during the summer. U.S. citizenship is required, and a valid email address is required to apply. Preferred: previous Hill, political or government office experience. Salary range: $44,988 to $69,412, with final pay depending on experience and qualifications.
Application requirements: Applicants must provide their school name, degree program and major, anticipated graduation date, current academic level, and overall GPA on a 4.0 scale, and must upload a copy of unofficial transcripts. Applications missing requested information may be disqualified.
Logistics: The application deadline is Sunday, November 1, 2026. The role is 40 hours per week on site. Telework and relocation assistance are not available, though housing assistance may be available.

item.title: Research Intern (Summer 2027)
item.description:
CNA is hiring a Research Intern for Summer 2027 at its Arlington, Virginia location. Interns are embedded in real study teams and either take on a self-contained research project or support multiple ongoing studies, applying rigorous analysis to real-world defense and security challenges. The role offers hands-on experience, mentorship, and networking opportunities in a collaborative, mission-driven environment.
Key responsibilities: Assist in defining and structuring analytical problems. Develop sound analytical techniques. Carry out analyses to logical conclusions. Communicate results both in writing and orally. Collaborate with expert researchers and analysts on complex national security issues. Contribute to projects that inform defense policy and operations. Present findings and insights to internal teams and potentially external stakeholders. Perform other duties as assigned.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree in the physical sciences, engineering, operations research, mathematics, statistics, economics, international relations, or a related discipline. Applicants must be enrolled in a graduate program (master's or PhD) and have a strong interest in policy research, national defense, or security studies. Undergraduate research experience, including literature searches, analyses, and report writing, is required, and graduate-level coursework and experience are preferred. Required skills include experience with database manipulation and Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), good interpersonal and oral and written communication, critical thinking, and organizational skills. Applicants must be able to obtain and maintain a security clearance, and U.S. citizenship is required.
Application and logistics: Apply by November 30, 2026. Preference is given to candidates who upload a resume, a cover letter describing their experience and why they want to intern with CNA, and transcripts (unofficial copies are accepted). The position is eligible for telecommuting or hybrid work at the supervisor's discretion, and interns may be required to work at CNA headquarters or other locations. All applicants are subject to a background investigation.

item.title: Internship
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/09/2026.
PIRG is a consumer advocacy organization working on solutions to problems that affect health, safety and well-being. It is hiring interns to work with its issue advocacy teams and its state offices across the country; the posting lists the department as Program and State and the workplace type as hybrid. Interns learn the basics of organizing and put those skills to work on public interest issues including consumer protection, public health, transportation, plastic pollution and more.
What interns do: Help educate and engage people on PIRG's issues, whether by getting issues into the media, helping grow coalitions, or organizing events, to build the public support needed to win. Learn how to analyze problems, push for smart solutions, and build public support for PIRG's goals. Work side-by-side with a staff member, learning the ropes. Attend briefings and trainings to learn more about the issues and gain organizing skills.
Who should apply: People who care deeply about solving these issues and are ready to make a difference now. The posting describes the internship as one of the best ways to gain experience for a career in political advocacy. No specific degree or experience requirements are listed.
Logistics: Interns are hired nationwide for fall, spring and summer terms. Applicants should indicate on the application which office or offices, and which term, they are applying for. Applications are accepted on a rolling basis. Internships are unpaid. PIRG is an equal opportunity employer.

item.title: Summer Research Assistant, Responsible Investing - Y Analytics
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/09/2026.
TPG is a leading global alternative asset management firm, founded in San Francisco in 1992, investing across private equity, impact, credit, real estate and market solutions. Y Analytics is TPG's internal capability for understanding and improving the environmental and social impacts of deployed capital. It supports impact assessment for The Rise Fund, the TPG Rise Climate Fund and other TPG vehicles, as well as responsible investing and sustainability across TPG and its portfolio. The Responsible Investing Research Assistant supports academic and industry research and analysis of the social impact of existing and potential investments, prepares thought leadership, and helps drive improved performance on responsible investing and sustainability factors across TPG's global portfolio.
Key responsibilities: Contribute to fast-paced teams conducting research, deal work and engagement with portfolio companies on responsible investing topics, including human capital management, external stakeholder relations, environmental health and safety, climate and other sustainability topics. Conduct and synthesize market research. Support academic and industry research on social impact. Prepare thought leadership.
Qualifications: Authorization to work in the U.S. (employment-based immigration sponsorship is not available). Undergraduate student who has completed at least two years of study, or a graduate student, pursuing a degree in Environmental Sciences, Environmental Engineering, Environmental Sustainability, Business, Economics, Public Administration or another relevant program. Experience or demonstrated interest in responsible investing, corporate social responsibility, climate/sustainability, consulting, finance, impact investing or a related field. Ability to use AI-enabled research and productivity tools effectively, responsibly and with appropriate judgement. Excellent Excel and PowerPoint skills. Excellent written and spoken communication skills and fluency in English. Experience with sustainability performance assessment or reporting frameworks (e.g., SASB, GRI) is a plus.
Compensation and logistics: $22.50 per hour, 40 hours per week, early June to late August 2027. The role is remote, and interns must be located during the internship in one of the following: AZ, CA, DC, FL, GA, IL, NJ, NY, TN, TX, VA, WI, AR, CO, IN, KY, LA, MA, MI, MN, MO, NE, NH, NC, OH, PA, SC, UT, WA, WY. In-person work may be an option for those near a TPG office.
How to apply: Instead of a cover letter, submit a written response of no more than one page (excluding citations) to the prompt in the posting. Choose a responsible investing theme, explain why it matters to investors or companies, synthesize one or two findings or debates, identify risks, opportunities or implementation considerations, and pose one question that deserves further research. Use standard document formatting and cite sources. Only applications submitted through the TPG careers page (https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/tpgcareers) will be considered.

item.company: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
item.title: 2026 CDC Public Health Fellowships
item.description:
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) supports education, training and development across the public health workforce, including postgraduate experiential service-learning fellowships. Its Public Health Fellowships prepare fellows to protect the nation's health, filling workforce gaps in epidemiology, policy, economic analysis, data science, laboratory science, public health service delivery and more. Three fellowships are currently accepting applications, and most are based in Atlanta, GA. This listing was published by ProFellow on behalf of CDC.
The fellowships: (1) Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program: paid 2-year applied training for doctoral- or master's-prepared professionals, applying computer science, data analytics and data science to public health needs. (2) Steven M. Teutsch Prevention Effectiveness (PE) Fellowship: a paid 2-year postdoctoral research fellowship in quantitative policy analysis, health economics-based inquiry and integrative health services research, assessing the effectiveness, quality and cost of public health policies, programs and practices. (3) Evaluation Fellowship Program: a paid 2-year fellowship for master's and doctoral recipients in which fellows build evaluation skills while helping their host program build, expand or improve its evaluation activities.
Qualifications: These are postgraduate programs. Informatics requires a doctoral or master's degree, the Prevention Effectiveness Fellowship is postdoctoral, and the Evaluation Fellowship is for master's and doctoral recipients. Each fellowship has its own detailed eligibility requirements, which are on CDC's fellowships webpage and not in this listing.
Compensation and benefits: Salary depends on the fellow's degree (master's or doctorate), with a posted range of $84,238 to $100,964. Benefits include health, vision and dental coverage, retirement benefits, and annual and sick leave.
Deadlines: Public Health Informatics Fellowship Program: applications are open through November 6, 2026. Prevention Effectiveness Fellowship: open through January 8, 2027. Evaluation Fellowship Program: opens October 26, 2026 and closes January 7, 2027. Application components vary by fellowship; see CDC's Public Health Fellowships website for details.

item.company: U.S. Department of Transportation (Office of the Secretary)
item.title: 1DOT Internship Program (Pathways)
item.description:
The U.S. Department of Transportation's 1DOT Pathways Internship Program lets aspiring public servants work directly on the operational and policy challenges shaping modern government. Interns are placed across DOT, where they work with engineers, analysts, economists, financial experts, human resources specialists and other professionals to advance national transportation initiatives. The program is expected to begin May 30, 2027, and the temporary appointment is not to exceed September 19, 2027, with a possible extension through the academic year if the intern remains eligible. The program integrates on-the-job training with education at an accredited institution.
Key responsibilities depend on the assigned office and may include: engineering, mathematics, IT, analytical and administrative assignments that build skills and practical experience; assignments that orient and train students in engineering, IT, mathematics, business, economics, management analysis, financial management, safety oversight, human resources, administrative support or transportation program operations; assisting professionals, analysts and program staff with planning, design, maintenance, operation, review and interpretation of business, engineering, mathematics or IT projects related to transportation; and helping develop briefings, reports, presentations, policy documents, communications products, conference materials and executive summaries for leadership. Occupational series include economics, financial management, safety inspection, transportation, information technology, human resources, administrative support, business and industry, community planning, environmental protection, engineering, and mathematics and statistics.
Qualifications: U.S. citizenship is required, and applicants must be at least 16. Students must be enrolled or accepted for enrollment at least half-time at an accredited college, trade school or other qualifying program for Fall 2027, and must keep a 2.5 cumulative GPA. Education levels by grade: GS-03, one academic year of post-high school study; GS-04, two years or an associate's degree; GS-05, four years leading to a bachelor's degree; GS-07, one year of graduate study or superior academic achievement. Students graduating before May 31, 2027 are not eligible unless accepted into an additional qualifying program. Transcripts are required with the application. Preferred fields include engineering, mathematics/statistics, IT, economics, business, public administration, finance, accounting, human resources, communications, management, data analytics and transportation.
Compensation and logistics: Salary is $32,435 to $77,306 per year (GS 3-7). The role is part-time or full-time, with at least 40 hours per week expected in the summer and a flexible part-time schedule during the school year. Interns report to an on-site location, and situational telework may be available. Vacancies are open in 32 locations: Little Rock, AR; Los Angeles, CA; Lakewood, CO; Hartford, CT; Washington, DC; Tallahassee, FL; Atlanta, GA; Ames, IA; Chicago and Matteson, IL; Lake Charles, LA; Cambridge, MA; Lansing, MI; Tupelo, MS; Trenton, NJ; Massena and New York, NY; Columbus, OH; Oklahoma City, OK; Salem, OR; Harrisburg, PA; San Juan, PR; Columbia, SC; Sevierville, TN; Austin, Dallas and Fort Worth, TX; Salt Lake City, UT; Ashburn and McLean, VA; Vancouver, WA; and Madison, WI. Applications are open October 21 to November 3, 2026, and must be submitted by 11:59 PM Eastern on the closing date. Interns may be converted non-competitively to a permanent position, up to GS-12, after meeting all Pathways requirements.

item.company: U.S. Department of Defense (Warfighting Acquisition University)
item.title: STUDENT TRAINEE (OPERATIONS RESEARCH)
item.description:
The DoW College Acquisition Internship Program (DCAIP), run through the Department of Defense's Warfighting Acquisition University, is a paid 10- to 12-week summer internship that gives students real-world exposure to Department of War acquisition workforce careers. It targets full-time second- and third-year undergraduates. This posting is for a Student Trainee (Operations Research) (series 1599, Mathematics and Statistics Student Trainee). Duties depend on your major and the program office where you are placed, based on the office's function and your skills and interests.
Key responsibilities: Gain hands-on, practical experience in analysis, research, report writing, oral briefings, policy development, program analysis and computer applications. Explore career fields in the acquisition workforce, including engineering, contracting, logistics, business (financial management and cost estimating), information technology, test and evaluation, industrial contract property management, purchasing, science and technology, production, quality and manufacturing, facilities engineering, and program management.
Qualifications: U.S. citizenship is required. Applicants must be enrolled full-time as a sophomore or junior in an undergraduate program at an accredited college or university and have completed at least 24 credit hours toward a specific degree program. A cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is required at the time of application and throughout the internship. Applicants must be suitable for federal employment, determined by a background investigation, and be able to obtain and hold a security clearance. Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered or exempt from Selective Service. A pre-employment drug test may be required. Transcripts (official or unofficial) must be submitted with the application, along with proof of full-time enrollment. Students graduating before May 31, 2027 are not eligible unless accepted into an additional qualifying degree program.
Compensation and logistics: Salary is $37,370 to $55,183 per year (GS-4). Telework is not available. Positions are in several locations: Redstone Arsenal, AL; Los Angeles County, CA; Colorado Springs, CO; Patrick AFB, FL; Wright-Patterson AFB, OH; Arlington, VA; and Fort Belvoir, VA. Applications are open October 1 to November 2, 2026, and close at 11:59 PM Eastern on the closing date, or earlier if 500 applications are received. The appointment is in the excepted service, and the position may be converted non-competitively to permanent employment after the intern completes their education.

item.company: U.S. Department of Agriculture (Farm Service Agency)
item.title: Student Trainee (Administration)
item.description:
The Farm Service Agency (FSA), part of the U.S. Department of Agriculture, is hiring Pathways student interns through the Deputy Administrator for Field Operations. Positions are filled under the Pathways Student Internship Authority, which provides paid work opportunities in federal agencies while students are in school. This administrative role supports the programs of an assigned FSA division.
Key responsibilities: Assemble PowerPoint presentation packages for division briefings. Type and prepare Microsoft Word documents for the division. Assist division members with a variety of special projects. Perform routine office and technical work that supports the administration or operation of the division's programs. Use Microsoft Access databases and Excel spreadsheets for data entry, editing, report creation, and monitoring and tracking of activities and efforts.
Qualifications: U.S. citizenship or U.S. national status is required. Students must be enrolled or accepted for enrollment at least half-time in an accredited technical or vocational school, college, university, graduate or professional school, and be pursuing a degree or certificate in or related to the internship field, such as business, business administration, finance, economics, accounting, human resources, information systems or public administration. Interns must stay in good academic standing (minimum 2.5 GPA), complete at least 480 hours of work experience before completing their degree, and sign a Pathways participant agreement. Education levels by grade: GS-02, high school or GED; GS-03, one full academic year of post-high school study; GS-04, two full academic years. Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered or exempt from Selective Service. Applicants must pass a background check and E-Verify, and a trial period of up to two years applies. A transcript and a resume of no more than two pages are required.
Logistics: Salary is $35,749 to $48,535 per year (GS 2-4), full-time, with occasional travel. Duty locations are negotiable within FSA's Northeast Region (CT, DE, ME, MD, MA, NH, NJ, NY, PA, RI, VT and WV) and are discussed at the interview stage. Telework is available as determined by agency policy, and this is a bargaining unit position. Applications are open October 19 to November 17, 2026, and must be submitted by 11:59 PM Eastern on the closing date. Interns may be converted to a term, career-conditional or career appointment within 180 days of completing their education, up to the GS-09 level, if they meet all Pathways requirements; conversion is not guaranteed. The posting lists GS-0301 as an example conversion series.

item.company: Bureau of Indian Affairs (U.S. Department of the Interior)
item.title: Student Trainee (Administration and Office Support)
item.description:
The Bureau of Indian Affairs (BIA), part of the U.S. Department of the Interior, is hiring Pathways interns, also called Student Trainees, who fill a wide variety of roles and functions in the offices and programs to which they are assigned. This is an open continuous announcement: applications are accepted and reviewed every two weeks until the posted closing date of January 29, 2027 (the announcement opened July 31, 2026). Interns learn about the nation-to-nation relationship between the federal government and federally recognized Tribal Nations and how BIA and Tribal Nations work together to oversee, protect, manage and use Indian Trust Lands and restricted lands.
Key responsibilities and training: Receive formal and on-the-job training to develop the knowledge and skills needed for entry-level positions within BIA. Be mentored by higher-graded employees and specialists in a specific specialty area. Receive developmental assignments that broaden knowledge of BIA activities and expand or deepen understanding of the intern's chosen specialty area within BIA.
Qualifications: U.S. citizenship is required. Education requirements under the GS-0399 Administration and Office Support Student Trainee standard are: GS-2, completion of high school or a GED; GS-3, one academic year of post-high school study; GS-4, two academic years of post-high school study or an associate's degree. Applicants must be students accepted for enrollment or enrolled and seeking a degree, diploma or certificate at a qualifying educational institution on a full- or half-time basis. Certificate programs must be at least one year of full-time post-secondary study. Students without a transcript, such as first-year or returning students, can submit a degree plan or other proof of enrollment, such as a course schedule, registration record, advisor-approved degree checklist or acceptance letter on official letterhead. All qualification requirements must be met by the closing date.
Conditions of employment: A one-year probationary period or two-year trial period applies. A background security investigation is required. Males born after 12/31/1959 must be registered with Selective Service. The incumbent may need to operate a government vehicle, which requires a valid driver's license and a safe driving record for the past four years.
Compensation and logistics: Salary is $29,725 to $47,334 per year (GS 2-4, Rest of U.S. rate; actual pay follows the scale for the selected location). Students may work full-time (40 hours per week) or part-time (16 to 32 hours per week). Duty location is negotiable after selection. Telework is not available.

item.title: Pickering, Rangel and Payne Fellowships (2027 Cycle)
item.description:
The U.S. Department of State is reestablishing the Thomas R. Pickering, Charles B. Rangel and Donald M. Payne Fellowships to streamline and unify these statutorily mandated Foreign Service recruitment and onboarding pathways. Through graduate education, professional development, mentorship, and domestic and overseas internships, the initiative aims to identify exceptional American talent and prepare a cadre of Foreign Service Officers. Fellows must complete a two-year master's degree program at a Department-approved university in the Washington, DC area and commit to a five-year service agreement with the Department after completing the fellowship and meeting entry requirements.
What the fellowship includes: graduate education, professional development, mentorship, a cohort experience in Washington, DC, and domestic and overseas internships, with updated academic support and financial assistance for the 2027 cycle. The posting does not list specific dollar amounts.
Eligibility: Applicants must be U.S. citizens with an undergraduate degree who are seeking admission to a two-year master's program in international affairs, public policy, development or a related field at an approved institution. A cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.2 or higher on a 4.0 scale is required at application, and the bachelor's degree must be completed before the fellowship begins. Applicants must be prepared to obtain and maintain Department of State medical, security and suitability clearances. For the 2027 cycle only, conditional offers will be made pending successful completion of the Foreign Service Officer Test (FSOT) and the written exercise of the Foreign Service Officer Assessment (FSOA).
Estimated 2027 timeline (from the posting): FSOT registration runs September 10 to October 30, 2026 and December 31, 2026 to February 5, 2027. The FSOT testing windows are October 10 to 31, 2026 and January 30 to February 6, 2027, and applicants must take the FSOT in one of those windows to meet the application deadline. The application period is December 2026 to January 2027. Candidates are notified in March 2027, finalist interviews are held in Washington, DC in March 2027, offers go out in April 2027, orientation is in June 2027, and the two-year graduate program begins in fall 2027. The Payne Fellowship application details were still forthcoming at the time of the posting.

item.title: Pathways to Public Service Fellowship
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/09/2026.
The City of Raleigh operates Partnership Raleigh, which brings together City departments to give college and university students introductory professional development opportunities while they explore careers in public service. The Pathways to Public Service Fellowship is a cohort-based, paid fellowship for college juniors, seniors, graduate students and recent graduates ages 18 to 30. Fellows are placed in City of Raleigh departments, where they contribute to projects, build professional skills, and gain firsthand insight into municipal government through structured professional development, mentorship and cross-departmental collaboration.
Key responsibilities: Work with City staff in departments that could include the City Manager's Office, Community Engagement, Housing and Neighborhoods, Sustainability, Transportation, Stormwater, Planning and Development, Solid Waste Services, Engineering Services, Procurement, IT, and Parks, Recreation, and Cultural Resources. Identify and address issues, and complete a capstone project that offers improvements or solutions in local governance. Use problem-solving and critical thinking to deepen understanding of local government operations and decision-making.
Qualifications: Experience with Microsoft Office and databases, and the ability to use Microsoft Teams. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and in a fast-paced team. Strong organization and attention to detail. Access to a computer, reliable internet and reliable transportation for commuting. Preferred: strong problem-solving and adaptability, professionalism and discretion, and living, working or studying in Raleigh or the Triangle region (not required). Strong candidates often major in political science, public administration, business, urban planning, policy, economics, sociology, psychology, environmental science, communications, IT, social work, criminal justice, geography, data analytics, engineering, or parks, recreation and tourism, though all majors are encouraged to apply.
Logistics: Fellows work 15 to 30 hours per week during a five-month fellowship from March 1, 2027 through August 6, 2027. Applications must include a resume, an essay of at least 200 words answering two prompts (how the fellowship will benefit your career aspirations, and what strengths, experiences or perspectives you would bring to your department and cohort), and a letter of recommendation. Applications missing any of the three items will not be reviewed. The posting does not state a pay amount.

item.title: Research Assistant
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/09/2026.
The Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago's Research Assistant Program is a two-year, full-time opportunity for recent graduates who want to see how economic research informs real-world policy. Research Assistants work alongside economists and researchers on questions facing the economy, financial markets, businesses and households, and contribute to both long-term research and timely policy analysis. RAs go on to graduate study in economics, public policy, finance, law and data science, or to careers in government, academia and industry.
Key responsibilities: Collect, clean, manage and analyze economic and financial data. Conduct statistical and econometric analysis and develop research code in tools such as Stata, R, Python and MATLAB. Conduct literature reviews and synthesize academic and policy research. Prepare charts, tables, written analysis, presentations and briefing materials. Support research papers, publications and time-sensitive policy analysis. Collaborate with economists, researchers and other Research Assistants across macroeconomics, microeconomics, finance and regional economics projects.
Qualifications: A bachelor's degree or higher in economics, finance, statistics, mathematics, computer science, data science, public policy or a related field, with strong economics and mathematics coursework. Strong quantitative, analytical and problem-solving skills. Familiarity with statistical programming languages such as Stata, R, Python or MATLAB. Strong written and verbal communication, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively. Curiosity, initiative and demonstrated interest in economics, research or public policy. Research experience is valued but not required.
Development and benefits: Training in programming, econometrics and data analysis; research seminars with Chicago Fed economists and visiting scholars; workshops, conferences and coursework; mentorship focused on graduate study and career planning; and opportunities to contribute to Chicago Fed research and publications, including potential joint authorship. The position is full-time with a competitive salary and benefits; the posting does not state a salary.
How to apply: Apply through the Chicago Fed's Workday portal. Upload a resume, cover letter, undergraduate transcript (unofficial is acceptable) and two references on the same page as the resume, because there is no separate upload prompt. At least one letter of recommendation must be sent directly by the recommender to ResearchAssistantLOR@chi.frb.org with your LAST NAME, FIRST NAME in the subject line. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Questions can go to RA.Recruiting@chi.frb.org.

item.title: Government Relations Intern [2027 Internship Program]
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 11/09/2026.
As a Government Relations Intern on DTCC's Government Relations team, you support the department's work with internal business lines, lawmakers, regulators and trade associations on legislative and regulatory policy issues affecting DTCC and the financial services industry. You gain practical exposure to policy research, legislative analysis, stakeholder engagement, written communications and DTCC Political Action Committee (PAC) activities, while learning how financial markets operate behind the scenes. The role is part of DTCC's 10-week Summer Internship Program, which includes orientation, training, mentorship, mid-point and final feedback, networking and development experiences that help students explore full-time career paths.
Key responsibilities: Monitor and flag news, legislation, hearings, regulatory developments and industry events affecting financial services. Watch and summarize congressional and state legislative hearings and industry events on topics such as financial regulation, financial technology, market structure, data privacy, cybersecurity and market resiliency. Support PAC activities by preparing written political updates, assisting with PAC Board presentations and helping prepare for meetings with Members of Congress. Research and analyze proposed legislation for its potential impact on DTCC, and help prepare subject matter experts for congressional meetings through research and briefing memos. Attend internal and external stakeholder meetings, capture notes and follow-ups, and support communications.
Qualifications: Currently pursuing a bachelor's degree in political science, history, constitutional law, economics, business, English literature or a related field, with an expected graduation date of Spring 2028 and a minimum GPA of 3.2. Authorization to work permanently in the United States without current or future sponsorship. Preferred: coursework, projects or experience in politics, public policy, financial markets, financial regulation or financial services; strong interest in those areas; and proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Word, PowerPoint and Excel. Law students with an interest in legal research and writing on legislative or regulatory proposals are also welcome.
Logistics: Competitive hourly compensation (the posting does not state a rate). Hybrid work model, with three days in the office and two days remote, based on team schedule.
